name: VTAB
description: Representation learning promises to unlock deep learning for the long tail of vision tasks without expansive labelled datasets. Yet, the absence of a unified yardstick to evaluate general visual representations hinders progress. Many sub-fields promise representations, but each has different evaluation protocols that are either too constrained (linear classification), limited in scope (ImageNet, CIFAR, Pascal-VOC), or only loosely related to representation quality (generation). We present the Visual Task Adaptation Benchmark (VTAB): a diverse, realistic, and challenging benchmark to evaluate representations. VTAB embodies one principle: good representations adapt to unseen tasks with few examples. We run a large VTAB study of popular algorithms, answering questions like: How effective are ImageNet representation on non-standard datasets? Are generative models competitive? Is self-supervision useful if one already has labels?
typical_sota_score: varies by subtask; aggregate top methods roughly 70–85%
reputation: Widely adopted in the vision community as a standard benchmark for evaluating general visual representations and few-shot adaptation across diverse tasks.
notes: Multi-task few-shot evaluation across many vision datasets; results depend heavily on pretraining data and potential ImageNet/pretraining contamination. Not an LLM benchmark; different subtasks have widely varying difficulty and saturation levels.
